name: openbrowser
description: CodeAgent MCP server with stateless web_search, explicit contexts, persistent namespaces, and isolated browser profiles
long_description:
OpenBrowser CodeAgent exposes seven tools to 2026-07-28 MCP clients, including stateless web_search and scrape_web. The web_search tool returns title, URL, and a discovery preview snippet without starting a browser or requiring a context_id. Scrape and read source pages before citing them. create_context returns a server-minted context_id; later stateful calls pass that handle explicitly. execute_code runs Python with browser automation functions in a persistent per-context namespace. Older clients that negotiate 2024-11-05 through 2025-11-25 receive a four-tool catalog, including web_search, and a legacy no-handle context.

### Key Features:
- **OpenBrowser web_search**: Discover sources with DDGS. Result snippets are discovery previews.
- **No-Browser Scrape**: scrape_web fetches static HTTP pages with no Blink or V8 process. It performs an HTTP fetch and parses the response; JavaScript is outside its scope.
- **Explicit Contexts**: Modern clients create, use, and close isolated application contexts with an explicit handle
- **Code Execution**: Write Python code with browser functions; most are async (await navigate, click, evaluate, etc.)
- **Persistent Namespace**: Variables and state persist between execute_code calls within one context
- **Recovery Tools**: get_status reports lifecycle and tab state without starting a browser; reset_browser closes a stuck browser while preserving scalar and scalar-only container variables by default
- **Isolated Resources**: Each context has its own managed profile, workspace, default downloads directory, namespace, and locks
- **Legacy Compatibility**: Older stdio clients keep four tools, including stateless web_search
- **Browser Automation**: Full browser control via CodeAgent functions
- **JavaScript Evaluation**: Run JS in page context via evaluate()
- **Data Libraries**: numpy and pandas are bundled; matplotlib, BeautifulSoup, pypdf, and tabulate are available only when installed
- **Standard Libraries**: json, csv, re, datetime, asyncio, Path

tools.name: create_context
tools.description: Create an isolated OpenBrowser context and return its context_id. No browser starts until the first execute_code call.

tools.name: execute_code
tools.description: Execute Python code in a persistent namespace with browser automation functions (navigate, click, evaluate, etc.). All functions are async; use await.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Return OpenBrowser server, browser, profile, and tab state as JSON. Read-only and does not start a browser.

tools.name: reset_browser
tools.description: Close the current browser session and release its profile. Scalar and scalar-only container variables are preserved unless clear_variables is true. Inspect namespace_transfer.dropped. Cookies and localStorage survive because the profile is reused.

tools.name: close_context
tools.description: Close one OpenBrowser context and release its browser and profile. A successful close invalidates the handle.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web without starting a browser or requiring a context_id. Search snippets are discovery previews.

tools.name: scrape_web
tools.description: Fetch one HTTP(S) URL without starting a browser. This is the no-Blink, no-V8 mode: no JavaScript, screenshots, cookies, or browser fallback. Use execute_code for JavaScript pages.

prompts.name: scrape_data
prompts.description: Extract structured data from a website
prompts.text: For a 2026-07-28 client, first call create_context and keep its context_id. Then use execute_code with that context_id to write Python that navigates to {url}, extracts data using evaluate() for JS DOM queries or Python string processing, and prints structured results. Call close_context when finished. Older clients call execute_code directly without a context_id.

prompts.name: fill_form
prompts.description: Fill out and submit a web form
prompts.text: For a 2026-07-28 client, first call create_context and keep its context_id. Then use execute_code with that context_id to navigate to {url}, get browser state to find form fields, and use input_text() and click() to fill and submit the form with: {field_data}. Call close_context when finished. Older clients call execute_code directly without a context_id.

prompts.name: research_topic
prompts.description: Research a topic across multiple websites
prompts.text: For a 2026-07-28 client, first call create_context and keep its context_id. Then use execute_code with that context_id to navigate to multiple sites, extract content using evaluate() or page text, and aggregate findings about {topic} using Python data structures. Call close_context when finished. Older clients call execute_code directly without a context_id.

workspace_directory.title: Workspace Directory
workspace_directory.description: Base directory for per-context file operations. Downloads use a separate per-context path.

headless.title: Headless Mode
headless.description: Run browser without GUI (faster, less memory). Set to false to see the browser window

user_data_dir.title: User Data Directory
user_data_dir.description: Optional explicit Chrome profile directory. Omit for an isolated profile per MCP server instance

storage_state.title: Storage State Path
storage_state.description: Optional JSON file used as a one-time seed for cookies plus localStorage in managed MCP profiles; later updates are saved to the active profile copy

allowed_domains.title: Allowed Domains
allowed_domains.description: Comma-separated list of domains the browser can access (e.g., 'example.com,*.google.com'). Leave empty for no restrictions

max_contexts.title: Maximum Contexts
max_contexts.description: Maximum open contexts total, including the legacy no-handle context
